Last opening: the full text of the July memo, from a plain-text mirror.I found one borderline candidate for 2014, and nothing about AGI or superintelligence.

**The candidate.** It's from Nadella's email to all employees on his first day as CEO, 4 February 2014. I read it on Microsoft's own Source site. He wrote: "I believe over the next decade computing will become even more ubiquitous and intelligence will become ambient." The next sentence says this will come partly from "intelligence from machine learning." It meets your rules: his own words, from that year, with a stated span. It's borderline because the forecast is more about computing in general than about AI hitting a specific milestone, so you may decide it doesn't count.

**Looked at and left out:**
- **27 March 2014 press briefing (official transcript):** he says "the world in the next five years and the 10 years is not going to be defined by the form factors that we know and love today". That's about device hardware, not AI. The line in the same speech about machine learning gives no date.
- **10 July 2014 memo, "Bold Ambition & Our Core":** I read it on a plain-text copy on a personal site, not Microsoft's own page. It says Cortana "in the future" will be "even more intelligent as a personal assistant". There's no date and it isn't about AGI, so it fits no list. Its "next few years" line is about new device types.
- **16 July 2014 partner conference keynote (official transcript):** the part I read has no dated AI forecast. The page was cut off before the end, so later passages are unchecked.
- **Skype Translator, Code Conference, May 2014:** the dated promise of a Windows 8 beta "before the end of 2014" is in a Microsoft blog post. Gurdeep Pall, who ran Skype, wrote it, not Nadella, so it isn't his claim.
- **CNBC interview transcript, 20 October 2014:** the page wouldn't open, so I don't quote it.
- **Video of his October 2014 Gartner interview and transcripts of the Code Conference conversation:** I didn't open these, so they stay unchecked.
